WITH order_counts AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) as order_count
  FROM "order"
  GROUP BY account_id
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) as overall_avg
  FROM order_counts
),
above_avg_accounts AS (
  SELECT oc.account_id, oc.order_count
  FROM order_counts oc, overall_stats os
  WHERE oc.order_count > os.overall_avg
),
above_avg_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) as above_avg_mean
  FROM above_avg_accounts
)
SELECT 
  aa.account_id,
  aa.order_count,
  aa.order_count - (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall_stats) AS above_overall_avg,
  aa.order_count - (SELECT above_avg_mean FROM above_avg_stats) AS above_above_avg_mean
FROM above_avg_accounts aa
ORDER BY above_above_avg_mean DESC
LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: "accounts with standing orders" means all accounts that appear in the order table (have at least one order), not a separate category of order types
"more orders than the average" uses strict inequality (>), not >=
